questions.q: Gray-black blotches of fungus growing on a painted wall are:
questions.n: Mildew thrives in damp, shaded areas.

questions.q: New concrete walls are still strongly alkaline. Which treatment is applied first so the paint film doesn't saponify and peel?
questions.n: A neutralizer counters the free lime in fresh concrete before primer and topcoat go on.

questions.q: Sandpaper coarseness is rated by:
questions.n: Higher grit numbers are finer.

questions.q: A cheap, alkyd-based, brush-applied rust-inhibiting primer for ordinary steel and iron is:
questions.n: Red oxide is the traditional low-cost general steel primer; zinc-rich and epoxy are higher-performance systems.

questions.q: The most durable, washable sheen is:
questions.n: Durability rises with sheen.

questions.q: Paint goes on best when relative humidity is around:
questions.n: High humidity slows drying and causes blush; very low humidity flashes it off.

questions.q: The usual paint for interior concrete walls and ceilings of a house is:
questions.n: Water-based latex is the standard interior wall and ceiling paint.

questions.q: Turpentine or mineral spirits would be the correct thinner for which of these coatings?
questions.n: Alkyd (oil-modified) paints are solvent-borne and thin with turpentine or mineral spirits.

questions.q: The paint ingredient that gives color and hides the substrate is the:
questions.n: Pigment gives opacity; binder forms the film.

questions.q: Tiny specks sticking up from a dried paint or varnish film, leaving it rough, are:
questions.n: Dust or skin particles trapped in the film.

questions.q: Painting a surface to imitate another material, like marble or wood grain, is a:
questions.n: Faux means false.

questions.q: A "duco" finish means the surface was sprayed with:
questions.n: Duco is the nitrocellulose automotive lacquer finish.

questions.q: For an exposed three-storey house, which topcoat best handles rain, sun and hairline cracking on the exterior concrete?
questions.n: Elastomerics flex and waterproof; they're the go-to exterior masonry topcoat.

questions.q: Which binder resin holds up best to UV on exterior concrete?
questions.n: Acrylic binders resist UV yellowing and chalking better than alkyds or oils.

questions.q: For exposed metal, the most sustainable finish is:
questions.n: Powder coating emits almost no VOCs, and overspray can be reclaimed.

questions.q: Baseboards, door casings and kitchen or bath walls take constant scrubbing. Which coating type do you specify?
questions.n: Enamel's hard film stands up to wear and repeated cleaning.

questions.q: The sheen between flat or matte and satin is:
questions.n: Eggshell has a faint luster.

questions.q: Liquid Tile is a ______ coating made by ______.
questions.n: Davies Liquid Tile is a solvent-borne acrylic masonry coating.

questions.q: Shellac is mainly used to:
questions.n: Shellac seals resinous knots and wood.

questions.q: A client wants a flat, non-shiny look on wood paneling with quick drying and good adhesion. Which suits best?
questions.n: Matte acrylics dry fast and give a flat sheen; the others are glossy finishes.

questions.q: For general exterior walls you want some durability, a soft sheen and good hiding of surface flaws. Which sheen?
questions.n: Satin balances washability against hiding imperfections; higher gloss shows every flaw.

questions.q: Which paint is laid on in very thick films and stays flexible enough to bridge hairline cracks on exterior masonry?
questions.n: Elastomerics are high-build, flexible exterior coatings.

questions.q: Pigment, binder, solvent and additives together make:
questions.n: Varnish and stain lack the opaque pigment load.

questions.q: Soap-like patches forming in the film, which then peels, are signs of:
questions.n: Alkali reacting with an oil binder.

questions.q: Which paint type doubles as a waterproofing coat?
questions.n: Elastomerics form a thick, flexible, water-shedding film.

questions.q: Primer for 148 m² of interior wall, one coat, and one 4-liter can covers about 25 m². How many cans do you order?
questions.n: 148 ÷ 25 = 5.92, rounded up to 6 cans.

questions.q: All of these can be thinned with water EXCEPT:
questions.n: Enamels are solvent-borne; latex, acrylic and emulsion paints are water-borne.

questions.q: A coastal mid-rise keeps blistering. The owner wants a solvent-based masonry coating (no water-based binder) that resists wind-driven rain on bare concrete. Which system fits?
questions.n: The brief excludes water-based binders, which rules out latex and elastomerics; a solvent-borne acrylic masonry system fits.

questions.q: Exterior metal grilles face sun, rain and frequent wiping. Which paint TYPE (not sheen) should be specified?
questions.n: Enamel cures to a hard, weather- and wash-resistant film suited to exterior metal.

questions.q: Fast-evaporating solvent plus resin binder, sprayed on fine wood furniture: this is ______.
questions.n: Lacquer dries by solvent evaporation and is the classic furniture finish.

questions.q: Sanding sealer is the right base when:
o: The wood will be painted opaque
The wood is for outdoor use
The final coat is a clear finish
questions.n: Clear finishes need a sealed, sanded base; paint takes primer.

questions.q: The undercoat whose job is to make the finish coat grip the surface, last longer and protect the substrate is the ______.
questions.n: A primer is the bonding and sealing undercoat of a paint system.

questions.q: Ornate cornices and trim highlights traditionally get which mirror-like finish?
questions.n: Super-gloss gives the glass-like reflection used to pick out decorative trim.

questions.q: Which color reflects the most solar radiation and keeps the wall surface coolest?
questions.n: White has the highest solar reflectance of the options.

questions.q: Paint film thickness is commonly expressed in:
questions.n: A mil is a thousandth of an inch; microns are also used.

questions.q: Steel columns need fire protection from a paint that swells into an insulating char when heated. Which?
questions.n: Intumescent paints expand into a carbonaceous foam that insulates the steel.

questions.q: Skim coat is usually sold in how many colors?
questions.n: White and gray versions.

questions.q: Xyladecor is applied to:
questions.n: It's a wood stain and preservative.

questions.q: Which coating cures by chemical reaction of a resin with a hardener, giving a hard enamel-like film that dries much faster than oil paint?
questions.n: Catalyzed (two-part) coatings cure chemically, so they harden faster than oxidizing oil/alkyd paints.

questions.q: Oil paint on fresh concrete can saponify, the alkali turning the binder soapy. So which is avoided on concrete?
questions.n: Alkaline concrete attacks oil binders; water-based latex is the usual concrete paint.

questions.q: Which finish is completely flat and best at hiding plaster irregularities?
questions.n: Matte scatters light, so surface defects show least.

questions.q: A pencil hardness test checks the hardness of:
questions.n: Graded pencils scratch the film.

questions.q: You're thinning an acrylic latex wall paint on site. What do you add?
questions.n: Latex and acrylic emulsions are water-borne, so water is the thinner; solvents would break the emulsion.

questions.q: Bare wood is being painted for the first time. Which goes on first to even out absorption and give the paint system a sound base?
questions.n: Wood primer seals the raw grain first; sanding sealer is the base for clear lacquer finishes, and filler only fills holes and grain.

questions.q: Textured wall finishes are usually done in:
questions.n: Water-based texture coats are easy to trowel and roll.

questions.q: On wood that will receive a clear lacquer finish, which coat goes under the topcoat to seal the grain and sand smooth?
questions.n: Sanding sealer seals and builds the surface so the lacquer topcoat lies even.
